waldensians.self: Sees itself as a Reformed church rooted in a Gospel renewal movement of the 1100s that joined the Reformation in 1532.

moravian.self: Sees itself as the Unity of Brethren, born of the Hussite reform before Luther, and one visible part of the body of Christ.

congregationalist.self: Sees itself as a Reformed tradition of churches gathered by covenant, each governed under Christ according to Scripture.

eastern-catholic.self: Sees itself as keeping the apostolic traditions of the ancient Eastern churches, handed down through the Fathers, in full communion with Rome.

quaker.self: Sees itself as reviving early Christianity through direct guidance from Christ, with baptism and communion understood as inward experiences.

old-believers.self: Holds that it keeps the Orthodox faith and rites handed down from the holy fathers, unchanged by the Russian reforms of the 1600s.

african-methodist-episcopal.self: Sees itself as part of Christ's universal church in the Methodist tradition, keeping its doctrine and worship despite separation over racial injustice.

latter-day-saints.self: Holds that after a widespread apostasy, the true Church of Jesus Christ was restored through Joseph Smith, with priesthood authority from heavenly messengers.

restorationist.self: Sees itself as restoring the New Testament church, uniting Christians on the Bible alone without creeds or denominational names.

holiness.self: Sees itself as recovering John Wesley's teaching of Christian perfection, calling believers to entire sanctification as a second work of grace.

adventist.self: Holds that, for Seventh Day Adventists, God calls a remnant to keep his commandments and the faith of Jesus amid widespread apostasy.

southern-baptist.self: Holds that a New Testament church is an independent congregation of baptized believers, keeping Christ's two ordinances under his lordship.

salvation-army.self: Sees itself as an international movement and an evangelical part of the universal Christian Church, preaching Christ and meeting human need.

jehovahs-witnesses.self: Holds that a great apostasy followed the apostles and that its own worldwide work is the foretold restoration of true worship.

old-catholic.self: Holds that it keeps the faith of the undivided church of the first millennium, with apostolic succession, and rejects Vatican I's papal dogmas.

national-baptist-convention.self: Holds that churches are congregations of baptized believers under Christ, with believers' baptism by immersion as the biblical pattern.

oneness-pentecostal.self: Holds that it preaches the apostles' message of Acts 2:38, one God revealed in Jesus and baptism in Jesus' name, as the Bible standard.
sources: Damick ch6: The Azusa Street Revival: The Spread of Pentecostalism

charismatic.self: Sees itself as a renewal inside the existing churches, spreading baptism in the Holy Spirit and spiritual gifts without forming a new church.

acna.self: Sees itself as part of the one, holy, catholic and apostolic church, keeping the Anglican Way of Scripture, creeds, bishops and the 1662 Prayer Book.

orthodox-church-ukraine.self: Sees itself as the historic Orthodox Church of Kyiv, now independent, keeping apostolic succession and communion with the Ecumenical Patriarchate.

global-methodist.self: Sees itself as part of the one, holy, catholic and apostolic church, preserving the historic Christian faith in the Wesleyan tradition.
